rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~72–76%; RBA Nov 3 hike to 4.85% ~81%; BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~94%; ECB Dec ~86%; BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~45%
rows.read: Most central banks still lean toward higher rates, and Australia and Britain are both expected to raise them this week. Oil's sharp fall eases some of the pressure behind those hikes, but none of the expected moves were priced out today. Currencies will move on whether banks hint at more.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US ISM manufacturing 55.5 (fcst 54.5), production 59.0; UK factory PMI 52.8 (5-month high); euro-area factory PMI 52.7
rows.read: Factories started the autumn strongly in the US and Britain, and euro-area industry kept growing. Solid growth gives central banks room to keep raising rates, which supports the dollar and the pound. Today it was outweighed by oil.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent settled $104.77 (−7.6%); ISM prices paid 75.2 (from 77.9); euro-area flash inflation Nov 4: forecast 4.0%
rows.read: Cheaper oil cut one of the main forces pushing prices up, and US factories reported costs rising a little more slowly. Inflation is still well above target in most big economies, so central banks have little room to relax yet. Euro-area figures on Wednesday are the week's main inflation test.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Hope for an end to the US–Iran war calmed energy markets, but US tech shares fell, so the mood was mixed. The Swiss franc drew the most shelter money, while the yen was held back by the wide gap in rates. Attacks on Gulf shipping continue, so the calm is fragile.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.read: Oil had one of its biggest one-day falls of the war after Iran backed peace talks. That shrinks the boost oil exporters like Canada get and eases the bill for importers like Japan and the euro area. Prices are still high by historical standards, and a failed deal could send them back up fast.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 27: funds strongly against CAD, against EUR (real money for), against NZD, for AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold (cut); oil net long among weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and the loonie held up today despite cheaper oil. They are also betting against the euro and the kiwi, while real money investors bet for the euro. Their large bets on gold are shrinking; new figures arrive Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Fitch: France A+, outlook negative (Oct 30); Moody's Aa3 negative; French revenue vote Nov 3; Canada budget Nov 5, 3:00 PM CT
rows.read: France's debt worries, with two rating firms on negative outlook, keep a weight on the euro. France's parliament votes on the revenue side of its budget on Tuesday, and Canada presents its budget on Thursday.
